title: Dynamic Disks via StorageClass
description:
**SITUATION:**

Earlier, someone had to **hand-register** archive disk before an app could use it. That does not scale when every team needs disks every week. Platform wants a **catalog entry**: “if an app asks for this kind of disk, create it automatically in the cloud / storage system.”

Your job is to publish that catalog entry, then prove it works by requesting a small disk and attaching it to a tiny helper Pod.

This lab publishes a **StorageClass** and proves dynamic provisioning with a PVC. No more hand-registering every archive disk — ask for a class, let the cluster create the volume.
**YOUR TASK:**

1. Create a **StorageClass** named `quickbyte-fast` (the catalog entry).
2. Create a storage request (**PVC**) that uses that class, plus a small consumer Pod so the disk can be created and bound.
3. Verify the claim becomes **Bound** (real disk appeared automatically — you did not hand-create a PV).

**SPEC:**

- StorageClass name: `quickbyte-fast`
- Provisioner: use what your lab cluster documents (authoring default for EKS: `ebs.csi.aws.com`) with:
  - `volumeBindingMode`: `WaitForFirstConsumer`
  - `reclaimPolicy`: `Delete`
  - parameters: `type: gp3` (when using EBS CSI)
- PVC name: `order-cache-pvc`
- Access modes: `["ReadWriteOnce"]`
- Storage request: `2Gi`
- `storageClassName`: `quickbyte-fast`
- Consumer Pod `cache-writer`: image `busybox:1.36`, mount PVC at `/cache`, command `sleep 3600`

**CONSTRAINTS:**

- StorageClass in `quickbyte-fast-sc-l22.yaml`; PVC + consumer Pod in `order-cache-pvc-l22.yaml`.
- Do **not** hand-create a PersistentVolume — let the class provision it.
- Work only in your lab namespace for namespaced objects.

hints: Your namespace is in the lab chrome and in $LEARNER_NS — kubectl already defaults there.
Work only in your lab namespace (not default).
Read SPEC carefully, apply your YAML, then Submit.
problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Dynamic Disks via StorageClass

Publish StorageClass `quickbyte-fast`, then request a PVC and attach it to a small consumer Pod so the provisioner can create the disk.

Docs: [StorageClasses](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/storage-classes/)

## Solution YAML

Save as `quickbyte-fast-sc-l22.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: quickbyte-fast
provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
reclaimPolicy: Delete
parameters:
  type: gp3
```

Save as `order-cache-pvc-l22.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: order-cache-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 2Gi
  storageClassName: quickbyte-fast
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cache-writer
spec:
  containers:
    - name: writer
      image: busybox:1.36
      command: ["sleep", "3600"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: cache
          mountPath: /cache
  volumes:
    - name: cache
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: order-cache-pvc
```

## Declarative

```bash
kubectl apply -f quickbyte-fast-sc-l22.yaml
kubectl apply -f order-cache-pvc-l22.yaml
kubectl get sc quickbyte-fast
kubectl get pvc order-cache-pvc
kubectl get pod cache-writer
```

Wait for the PVC to become **Bound** (when the CSI provisioner is available), then **Submit**. Do not hand-create a PersistentVolume.
